variants.headline: Party leader blunders in election debate
variants.sub: An election debate has included a blunder by a party leader.
variants.body:
A party leader has blundered in an election debate. The misstep is established, but the words involved and their effect on voters are not supplied here. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the debate event from a fabricated quotation or a claim that the election's outcome has been decided.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate.

variants.headline: A debate brings a leader's misstep
variants.sub: A party leader has made a misstep in an election debate.
variants.body:
An election debate has produced a leader's blunder. Public speaking is part of political leadership, though an awkward moment is not a complete political record. For {target}, the question is judgment under scrutiny, without inventing what was said or how the audience responded to the mistake.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate.

variants.headline: Election argument meets an awkward moment
variants.sub: A party leader has blundered in an election debate.
variants.body:
The colony's election argument includes a blunder by a party leader in debate. It is legitimate political news, not a substitute for the whole contest. An assessment of {target} should keep the misstep in proportion and leave polling changes or electoral consequences outside the factual account.

We criticise {target} in this assessment. Political leadership includes judgment under scrutiny, and a debate blunder is an appropriate occasion to question whether the standard of public presentation has been adequate.
